title: observability trace drop debug notes - priya wip
content:
Incident summary:
- 2025-11-10 03:12 UTC: alert firing: observability.trace_drop_rate > 0.05 (5% of incoming spans being dropped)
- Affected services: api-gateway, inference-runtime (high throughput); drop spikes correlated with background deploys but persisted after deploys finished.

What I saw (quick notes):
- Prometheus rule 'trace_drop_rate' jumped at 03:10 and stayed elevated for ~45m.
- Grafana dashboard shows ingestion lag for otel-collector (consumer backlog).
- Jaeger/Tempo: many traces missing spans (root present, many child spans dropped).
- Loki: no obvious spikes in log errors from otel-collector prior to 03:10, but after restart collectors logged "ERROR: failed to decode OTLP batch - resource limits hit"

Commands I ran (outputs trimmed):
- kubectl -n observability get pods
  otel-collector-0   1/1 Running   0    12d
  tempo-0            1/1 Running   0    5d

- kubectl logs -n observability deploy/otel-collector -c collector | tail -n 120
  2025-11-10T03:11:57Z ERROR otel_collector exporter/kafka: failed to produce message: kafka: message too large
  2025-11-10T03:12:12Z WARN  otel_collector pipeline: dropping span batch, reason: queue full

- curl -X POST http://localhost:4318/v1/traces -d @sample-otlp-batch.json -H 'Content-Type: application/octet-stream'
  -> POST accepted locally, but consumer group lag increased by ~2000

- kafka-consumer-groups --bootstrap-server kafka.observability.svc:9092 --group observability-ingester --describe
  CURRENT-OFFSET  LAG  CONSUMER-ID
  1248923         2200 consumer-1

- kubectl exec -n observability otel-collector-0 -- cat /etc/otel/config.yaml | sed -n '1,180p'
  receivers:
    otlp:
      protocols:
        grpc: {}
        http: {}
  processors:
    batch: {}
    memory_limiter:
      limit_mib: 512
      spike_limit_mib: 128
      check_interval: 5s
  exporters:
    kafka:
      brokers: ["kafka.observability.svc:9092"]
      topic: "otel-spans"
      max_message_bytes: 1000000

- kubectl top pods -n observability
  otel-collector-0   620m  1.8Gi
  tempo-0             240m  1.2Gi

Error snippets (copied):
- "failed to produce message: kafka: message too large"
- "dropping span batch, reason: queue full"
- "memory limiter triggered; rejecting spans"
- "ERROR: failed to decode OTLP batch - unknown resource schema"

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Configuration regression: max_message_bytes or batching changes in last deploy (PR #487) increased batch sizes -> kafka producers hitting max_message_bytes -> messages rejected -> queue fills -> spans dropped.
2) Memory pressure on otel-collector: memory_limiter configured to 512Mi but ingestion burst exceeded this -> processor started rejecting/ dropping.
3) Kafka broker-side retention or request-size limit decreased (ops or infra change) causing producer errors.
4) Sampling changes in instrumentation causing many large spans (compressed payloads bigger).

What I checked / evidence: 
- PR history: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/487 merged 2025-11-09 22:04 UTC - this PR increased batch size in pipeline config (batch/timeout changed).
- Config in cluster still shows max_message_bytes: 1000000 (1MB). Some generated spans ~800k uncompressed + OTLP overhead -> hitting 1MB after proto framing.
- Kafka broker logs around 03:11 show: "Request too large" on broker-2 (ops asked for more detail, awaiting logs).
- Resource usage: collector memory peaked ~1.8Gi -> memory_limiter tripped -> logs show "memory limiter rejecting spans"

Immediate mitigations tried:
- Rolled back PR #487 on staging earlier today (works), performed rollback to previous config in prod at 04:05 UTC -> drop rate returned to normal within ~3m. (Rollback notes in linked PR).
- Increased otel-collector deployment replicas from 1 -> 3 (kubectl scale deploy/otel-collector --replicas=3) to spread ingestion while rollback completing. Dropped lag but not fully fixed until rollback.
- Temporarily set kafka exporter.max_message_bytes to 2.5MB on a single collector for testing (hotfix) -> producer accepted batch, but not a long-term solution; also increased memory pressure.

Followups / TODOs:
- [ ] Audit recent config PRs for batching/size changes (owner: Arjun) -> reopen PR-487 review thread about safe defaults.
- [ ] Add a pre-merge CI step to simulate large-span batches and run producer Kafka checks (size, retries).
- [ ] Add alert: 'kafka_producer_message_rejects_total' or instrument exporter to export metric when producer returns 'message too large'.
- [ ] Tune memory_limiter config (increase limit to 2Gi on collectors) and test under load before rolling out.
- [ ] Put a collector-side post-processor to split very large spans/batches if feasible.
- [ ] Coordinate with infra for broker max.request.bytes and replica configs; increase broker-side limits if needed.

Notes / breadcrumbs for later:
- trace_id: 9f1b2d3a4c5e6f7890abcdeffedcba12 (example of dropped trace observed where child spans missing)
- correlate with log lines: kafka-broker-2 stderr 2025-11-10T03:11:58Z "Request too large from producer id: x"
- Related tickets: JIRA-OBS-1123 (incident), JIRA-OBS-1126 (postmortem/outage review)

Quick wins I can do today:
- Add metric emit for producer errors in kafka exporter (small code change)
- Increase memory_limiter to 1.5Gi on prod collectors behind feature flag for 24h to observe behavior
- Add a note to PR template reminding to consider kafka/exporter settings when changing batch config

Open questions:
- Why did the batch size increase so much? Is it instrumentation change at service side (many attributes, long sql statements in span)?
- Should we implement chunking at exporter level or enforce stricter per-span size limit?
- What's the long-term approach: smaller batches vs. increasing broker limits vs. splitting spans?

References:
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/487
- Incident ticket: JIRA-OBS-1123
- Quick repro: samples/sample-otlp-batch-large.json (attached to this doc in Drive)

Last edit notes: 2025-11-11 09:12 UTC - added broker log snippet from ops and confirmed rollback timeline.

-- Priya
